title: A01 Broken Access Control
body: Authorization failures, insecure direct object references, privilege escalation, path traversal, and server-side request forgery can indicate broken access control. A scanner observation alone is not proof that access can be bypassed; retain the affected route, role context, and safe evidence.

title: A02 Security Misconfiguration
body: Missing or unsafe security headers, default configurations, verbose errors, unnecessary services, and insecure platform settings may indicate security misconfiguration. Describe the observed configuration and affected response.

title: A03 Software Supply Chain Failures
body: Risks in dependencies, build systems, distribution, update mechanisms, and third-party software can indicate software supply chain failures. A version banner by itself is not proof of a vulnerable or compromised component; establish component identity and relevant advisory evidence.

title: A04 Cryptographic Failures
body: Weak or missing encryption, unsafe TLS configuration, exposed sensitive data, or poor key and secret handling may indicate cryptographic failures. State what was actually observed and avoid claiming data exposure without evidence.

title: A05 Injection
body: SQL, command, template, LDAP, and cross-site scripting injection findings generally map to Injection when untrusted input is interpreted as executable syntax. Include the input location, safe verification evidence, and affected context.

title: A06 Insecure Design
body: Insecure Design concerns missing or ineffective security controls arising from design decisions. It usually requires threat modeling or architectural evidence; automated scanner alerts alone rarely establish this category.

title: A07 Authentication Failures
body: Weak authentication, credential stuffing exposure, unsafe recovery flows, missing multifactor protections, and session-management failures may indicate authentication failures. Identify the tested account and flow without exposing credentials.

title: A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures
body: Failure to verify software, code, or data integrity can enable unauthorized modification, unsafe deserialization, or untrusted update behavior. Retain evidence of the trust boundary and integrity check that failed.

title: A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures
body: Insufficient security logging, monitoring, or alerting can delay detection and response. This generally requires review of logging behavior and operational controls; absence of a response header does not prove a logging failure.

title: A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
body: Improper error handling, failing open, unexpected state transitions, and exceptional-condition logic errors may indicate mishandling of exceptional conditions. Preserve the triggering condition and observed safe response.

title: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (conditional)
body: T1190 describes adversaries exploiting a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to gain initial access. A vulnerability finding or scanner alert alone must not be mapped as observed ATT&CK behavior. Include this only as a conditional candidate when assessment evidence demonstrates exploitation of a public-facing application; distinguish observed behavior from exposure or theoretical impact.
